extracted.intended_audience: investigative reporters, editors, and newsrooms submitting work for IRE Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used to judge investigative reporting entries for the IRE Awards; covers originality, documentation, data, storytelling, production, digital presentation, and public impact. Intended to guide journalists preparing submissions and judges evaluating entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantially the product of the reporter's own initiative and effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should be produced primarily through the reporter's own initiative and effort rather than being handed to the journalist by a source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes original reporting activity driven by the journalist; not simply republishing or reformatting material provided by insiders or sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncovering facts that someone or some agency may have tried to keep from public scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporting should expose facts that were concealed or not otherwise readily available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for revelations or exposure of hidden information, demonstrating investigation beyond publicly released materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues of public importance
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject matter should concern matters of significance to readers, viewers, or listeners — topics that affect the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges consider the public importance threshold when assessing impact and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enterprise — going beyond the press release / official announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting should demonstrate initiative beyond covering press releases or official statements; it should involve additional reporting and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks reporting that pursues leads, develops new angles, and does not rely solely on material originating from authorities or spokespersons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong paper trails and records supporting reported facts; thorough sourcing and documentary evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes quality and depth of documentation — records, documents, and other verifiable evidence that substantiate claims and findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in data
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate quantitative analysis and use of data to support findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses rigor and appropriateness of data analysis, including how data were obtained, processed, and interpreted; quantitative rigor where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates structure, clarity, pace, hooks, and narrative techniques that make the investigation readable and compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia and presentation craft supporting the reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers audio/visual production values, use of multimedia elements, and how presentation choices enhance comprehension and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the digital experience for online journalism entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes website/layout/usability choices, interactive elements, and how the digital format augments storytelling and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader/viewer involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the work generates engagement, action, or response from the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers measurable public reaction, engagement metrics, follow-up actions, or community response attributable to the reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening and judging process
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are initially reviewed by screeners; final judging is done by the IRE Awards Committee composed of IRE Board members and elected/appointed investigative journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a multi-stage review with experienced investigative journalists; relevant for entrants to understand evaluation workflow and potential reviewer expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Strict conflict-of-interest rules govern who may participate in judging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures impartiality of judges; entrants should be aware the committee follows COI policies to maintain fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden vs. public knowledge (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for work that uncovers what was concealed rather than merely recounting what was already public knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely related to 'uncovering facts' and 'original reporting' — judges value revelations that change public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public importance threshold (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges apply a threshold of public importance when evaluating whether an investigation merits recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every investigation qualifies; the topic must meet a bar of significance to the audience or public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original reporting (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should represent original reporting rather than re-aggregation of existing material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards new information, original analysis, or reporting that adds substantive new insights beyond synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation/evidence quality (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality supporting evidence and documentation are essential to substantiate claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlaps with 'Excellence in documentation' — judges will weigh the reliability, depth, and traceability of sources and records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling craft (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative skill and presentation quality factor into assessments of investigative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlaps with 'Storytelling' and 'Production' — judges consider how effectively the story communicates and keeps audience attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative rigor (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate methodological rigor in quantitative analyses supports credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to 'Excellence in data' — judges look for sound methods, transparency about limitations, and correct interpretation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public impact / response generated (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of public impact, policy change, or audience action resulting from the reporting strengthens an entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact can include official investigations, policy changes, public outcry, or measurable engagement attributable to the work.
